page: Amazon Web Services c5a.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 x86_64 processor, delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads. Memory allocation is configured at 4.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include standard AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, while AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets are absent. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, relying completely on external network-attached EBS volumes for persistence, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread efficiency contrasted with restricted multi-threaded capabilities due to its 2-vCPU envelope. The AMD core registers average performance in single-threaded tasks, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1263.0, gzip compression at 23.95 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 9.35 GB/sec. However, aggregate processing capabilities rank in lower percentiles across broader suites, posting 1593.0 on Geekbench multi-core, 2820.21 on PassMark CPU, and 767.58 on multi-core stress-ng tests. Memory throughput reflects entry-tier DDR4 bandwidth with 24.05 GB/sec uncached reads and 20.03 GB/sec writes, alongside Redis operations measuring 1.83 million operations per second and static web throughput of 2.19 GB/sec.

Positioned as an affordable alternative to Intel-based compute instances, the c5a.large provides dedicated CPU allocations without the variability of burstable credit models. The primary architectural tradeoff is the small resource ceiling of 2 vCPUs and 4 GB RAM, which restricts sustained multi-threaded parallelism and memory-dense workloads. The instance is suited for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale web serving, microservices, continuous integration build agents, and single-threaded data compression jobs.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.large is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro system, running a 3.3 GHz AMD EPYC 7R32 processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical core, paired with 4.0 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and features no local instance storage, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate respectable single-threaded execution, demonstrating average results in single-core Geekbench and compression tasks, but low multi-core and aggregate memory bandwidth outputs due to its small two-thread limit. Offering non-burstable dedicated CPU resources at a budget-friendly operational footprint, the c5a.large fits lightweight web applications, microservices, small CI/CD build workers, and routine batch processing tasks.
